name: McArthur River
note: Unconformity U at 500-640 m along the P2 reverse fault; production since 1999 plus reserves and resources ~ 750 Mlb U3O8 (~ 340 kt U3O8) at ~ 10 % average; ore in Paleoproterozoic basement and basal Athabasca sandstone

name: Cigar Lake
note: Flat unconformity lens 1950 m long and 25-100 m wide at 410-450 m; reserves ~ 216 Mlb at ~ 18 % plus Phase 2 resources ~ 300 Mlb U3O8 in all

name: Key Lake (Gaertner and Deilmann)
note: Two pits along one basement fault; produced ~ 209 Mlb U3O8 (1983-1997) at ~ 2 %; now the McArthur River mill

name: Rabbit Lake (Rabbit Lake + Collins Bay + Eagle Point)
note: Produced ~ 200 Mlb U3O8 1975-2016 from several unconformity and basement pods; tonnage and grade back-calculated

name: Arrow (Rook I)
note: Basement-hosted steep shear zones under ~ 100 m of sand; M&I 3.75 Mt at 3.10 % (256.7 Mlb) plus inferred 4.4 Mt at 0.82 % (80.6 Mlb) U3O8

name: Ranger (Nos 1 and 3)
note: Produced ~ 132 kt U3O8 1981-2021 at ~ 0.25-0.3 %; Ranger 3 Deeps resource added; Cahill Formation schists

name: Jabiluka
note: Undeveloped; Jabiluka 2 resource ~ 140-160 kt U3O8 at ~ 0.5 %; lenses dip moderately east in Cahill Formation

name: Beverley
note: In-situ leach roll-front in Miocene Namba Formation sands at 100-140 m; ~ 21 kt U3O8 original resource

name: Inkai (Chu-Sarysu)
note: ISR roll-fronts in Upper Cretaceous Inkuduk and Mynkuduk sands at 350-530 m; ~ 300 kt U (~ 375 kt U3O8) including production

name: Budenovskoye and Mynkuduk (Chu-Sarysu north)
note: Largest ISR field in the world; Budenovskoye ~ 270 kt U and Mynkuduk ~ 100 kt U in Cretaceous sands; positions approximate (centre of the field)

name: Uchkuduk
note: First Soviet sandstone U (1950s); open pit then ISR in Cretaceous sands of the Kyzylkum; ~ 60 kt U3O8 order of magnitude

name: Rossing
note: Low-grade alaskite (Damaran) in the Khan and Rossing formations; produced > 140 kt U3O8 since 1976 plus remaining resources ~ 260 kt U3O8 in all

name: Husab (Rossing South)
note: Alaskite zones 1 and 2 ~ 380 Mlb U3O8 (~ 172 kt) at ~ 0.04 %

name: Langer Heinrich
note: Calcrete in a Cenozoic palaeochannel (surficial); ~ 160 Mlb U3O8 incl. production; 0060 keeps uranium in bed or basement so the runtime puts it in the rock just under the valley fill

name: Arlit and Akouta (Tim Mersoi basin)
note: Somair (open pit) and Cominak (underground to ~ 250 m, closed 2021) in Carboniferous Guezouman and Tarat sandstones; produced ~ 145 kt U plus remaining

name: Imouraren
note: Undeveloped; ~ 200 kt U reserves at ~ 0.08 % in Jurassic Tchirezrine 2 sandstone

name: Elliot Lake (Blind River)
note: Quartz-pebble conglomerate (Huronian Matinenda Formation) on both limbs of the Quirke syncline; produced ~ 360 Mlb U3O8 1955-1996 at ~ 0.1 %

name: Streltsovsky ore field (Krasnokamensk)
note: ~ 19 vein and stockwork deposits in a Late Jurassic caldera; ~ 280 kt U pre-mining (~ 140 kt produced since 1968)

name: Jachymov (Joachimsthal)
note: Pitchblende veins in Paleozoic mica schist; ~ 7900 t U 1945-1964; silver from 1516 (the thaler); radium source for the Curies

name: Schlema-Alberoda
note: Largest vein U deposit in Europe: ~ 80 kt U (Niederschlema-Alberoda ~ 73 kt plus Oberschlema) mined to ~ 1800 m by SDAG Wismut 1946-1990

name: Pribram
note: ~ 48 kt U 1950-1991 from veins along the Central Bohemian pluton contact; shafts to ~ 1800 m

name: Shinkolobwe
note: Very rich pitchblende in Roan (Katangan) dolomitic shales; ~ 25-30 kt U3O8 mined to 1960 (Manhattan Project ore)

name: Oklo and Mounana (Franceville basin)
note: Paleoproterozoic Francevillian FA sandstone; ~ 28 kt U produced by COMUF 1961-1999; the natural fission reactors of 2 Ga

name: Jaduguda
note: Two lodes in the Singhbhum shear zone dipping ~ 40 deg; worked since 1968 at ~ 0.06 % U3O8

name: Ambrosia Lake (Grants mineral belt)
note: Tabular and redistributed ore in the Jurassic Morrison Formation (Westwater Canyon) at ~ 120-600 m; the main district of the Grants belt (~ 340 Mlb U3O8 in all)

name: Uravan mineral belt
note: U-V ore in the Jurassic Salt Wash member (Morrison Fm); ~ 70 Mlb U3O8 plus ~ 5x as much V2O5 (~1.5 %), the vanadinite share (iron-ferro gave this body to the uranium group)

name: Gas Hills
note: Roll-fronts in the Eocene Wind River Formation; ~ 130 Mlb U3O8 order of magnitude

name: Smith Ranch-Highland (Powder River basin)
note: ISR roll-fronts in the Eocene Wasatch and Paleocene Fort Union sands

name: Zhovti Vody (Kryvyi Rih-Kremenchuk belt)
note: Sodium-metasomatite (albitite) U in Paleoproterozoic rocks; mined since the 1950s

name: Kvanefjeld (Ilimaussaq)
note: Lujavrite REE-U-Zn resource 1010 Mt at 266 ppm U3O8 (~ 270 kt U3O8) incl. Sorensen and Zone 3; Mesoproterozoic Gardar intrusion

name: Borrowdale wad mine (Seathwaite)
note: The only lump (vein) graphite deposit worked at scale in Europe: pipes and veins in Ordovician Borrowdale Volcanic Group andesite; a few thousand tonnes in all from c. 1550 to 1891; pencils of Keswick

name: Bogala
note: Vein graphite (95-99 % C in the veins) in Highland Complex granulites; mined since the 19th century to ~ 600 m

name: Kahatagaha-Kolongaha
note: Second historic vein-graphite mine of Sri Lanka; position approximate (Kurunegala-Matale district)

name: Balama
note: Flake graphite in Neoproterozoic graphitic schist (Lurio belt); resource ~ 1.15 Gt at ~ 10 % TGC (reserves 114 Mt at 16 %)

name: Mahenge (Epanko-Ulanzi)
note: Flake graphite in Neoproterozoic Mozambique-belt gneiss; JORC resource ~ 212 Mt at 7.8 % TGC

name: Ancuabe
note: Flake graphite in Neoproterozoic gneiss; resource order 30 Mt at ~ 6 % TGC

name: Jixi (Liumao)
note: Largest Chinese flake graphite district in Paleoproterozoic Mashan Group; several hundred Mt of ore

name: Luobei (Yunshan)
note: Large Mashan Group flake graphite field; tonnage order of magnitude

name: Pingdu (Nanshu)
note: Shandong flake graphite in Paleoproterozoic Jingshan Group

name: Kropfmuehl (Passau)
note: Flake graphite in Moldanubian gneiss of the Bavarian Forest; graphite clay for Passau crucibles since the Middle Ages; underground mine since 1870

name: Kaisersberg (Styria)
note: Microcrystalline graphite in Carboniferous metasediments of the Veitsch nappe; mined since the 18th century

name: Skaland (Traelen)
note: Highest-grade flake mine in operation; Traelen resource ~ 1.8 Mt at ~ 22-28 % TGC in Precambrian gneiss

name: Weardale (North Pennine orefield)
note: Fluorite zone of the North Pennine orefield: veins and flats in Carboniferous (Great) Limestone; ~ 3 Mt fluorspar 1880-1999; medieval lead with fluorite gangue (the base-metals group places Pb)

name: Derbyshire (Peak District orefield)
note: Rakes pipes and flats in Carboniferous limestone; eastern fluorite belt and Castleton Blue John; ~ 5 Mt CaF2

name: Illinois-Kentucky fluorspar district (Cave-in-Rock and Rosiclare)
note: Bedded replacement (Cave-in-Rock) and fault veins (Rosiclare) in Mississippian limestone; ~ 12.7 Mt fluorspar 1835-1995, the largest US district

name: Muzquiz district (Coahuila)
note: Mantos replacing Cretaceous (Aurora) limestone at rhyolite contacts; position = centre of the district (best-guess table)

name: Las Cuevas (Villa de Zaragoza)
note: World's largest high-grade (acid-grade) fluorspar mine: replacement at a rhyolite-Cretaceous limestone contact; position approximate

name: Woelsendorf
note: Fluorite veins in Variscan granite and gneiss (basement); ~ 3 Mt fluorspar 1850-1987; 0060 keeps fluorite in beds so the runtime uses a similar host

name: Ivittuut cryolite
note: Cryolite (Na3AlF6) pipe in Gardar granite, the world's only large cryolite body: ~ 3.8 Mt ore mined 1854-1987; no cryolite block so it is placed as fluorite

name: Vergenoeg
note: Fayalite-magnetite-fluorite volcanic pipe in Bushveld (Rooiberg) felsites; the world's largest fluorite resource ~ 200 Mt at ~ 25-30 % CaF2

name: Marico fluorspar field (Witkop)
note: Stratabound fluorite in Paleoproterozoic Malmani dolomite (Transvaal Supergroup) north-east of Zeerust; position approximate

name: Okorusu
note: Fluorite replacing Damaran marble at a Cretaceous alkaline carbonatite complex; produced ~ 2 Mt since 1988

name: Wuyi fluorite district (Zhejiang)
note: Fault-fill fluorite veins in Jurassic-Cretaceous volcanics; China's main vein fluorspar field; host is volcanic so the runtime uses a similar bed host

name: Asturias fluorspar district (Caravia-Berbes)
note: Stratabound fluorite at the Permo-Triassic unconformity over Carboniferous limestone; Spain's main source

name: St. Lawrence (Newfoundland)
note: Fluorite veins in the Devonian St. Lawrence granite (basement); ~ 2 Mt produced 1933-1978 plus resources

name: Cristalina rock crystal
note: Rock crystal veins in Proterozoic quartzite; major piezoelectric quartz source in the 1940s

name: Diamantina rock crystal (Serra do Espinhaco)
note: Quartz veins and crystal pockets in Espinhaco quartzites

name: Ametista do Sul amethyst
note: Amethyst geodes in one Cretaceous Serra Geral basalt flow, worked by galleries; tonnage = geode quartz order of magnitude

name: Artigas amethyst
note: Amethyst and agate geodes in Cretaceous Arapey basalt flows

name: Spruce Pine high-purity quartz
note: Devonian alaskite (pegmatitic granite) with ~ 25 % quartz: the world's main high-purity quartz source; tonnage = alaskite worked and reserved

name: Ouachita quartz crystal belt (Mount Ida-Hot Springs)
note: Quartz-crystal veins in Ordovician-Mississippian sandstone and shale of the Ouachita Mountains

name: Aar massif cleft crystals (Grimsel-Goescheneralp)
note: Alpine clefts in Variscan Aar granite; crystal trade since the Middle Ages (Zinggenstock cleft 1719 ~ 50 t); a few thousand tonnes in all

name: Idar-Oberstein agate
note: Agate (chalcedony) amygdales in Permian Rotliegend volcanics; agate cutting recorded from 1454; tonnage order of magnitude
